verdict.rationale: The evidence shows no user-definable rule or workflow engine in Oyster that triggers actions automatically on events. Webhooks push event notifications to a developer's endpoint, which is a building block for constructing automation externally, not a rules-to-actions capability. The marketing phrases "powerful automations" and "Automated expenses, time-off" do not describe user-defined rules, so the verdict stays at none.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events
